prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity decision comp for a web-app redesign
Primary request: Create one 16:9 presentation image showing TWO complete Wicker Study desktop app screens side by side, Settings on the left and Documents on the right. Direction: Record & Revision Desk.
Input image: reference image supplies the exact Wicker Study app chrome, warm neutral canvas, narrow typography, indigo action color, flat ruled white panels, 14px major corners, sidebar proportions, density, and component character. Do not copy its Courses content.
Screen 1, Settings: persistent Wicker sidebar with Documents under MANAGE, page title "Settings", a small local settings navigation column, and a broad "Connections" work area. Show two full-width ruled vendor rows: Canvas with the actual red Canvas LMS logomark, status Connected, account origin, last sync and Manage action; Timetable with calendar/feed icon, status Connected, appointment count, refresh note and Manage action. Below show a quiet add-connection row. All internal dividers reach the panel edges.
Screen 2, Documents: persistent same sidebar with Documents active. Page title "Documents", short subtitle, Upload document primary action. Broad left registry lists "Transcript", "Academic Work", and "Academic calendar" as full-width ruled rows with type, current version, date, and state. Right selected-document pane shows "Transcript", v3 current, a small factual progress chart for credits earned and courses passed, then a vertical dated version rail with v3, v2, v1 and actions Replace, View details, Remove. Clear privacy note that parsed records are retained, not original PDFs.
Style/medium: production SaaS UI screenshot, crisp vector-like interface, not a poster and not a device mockup.
Composition: both screens large and readable, equal scale, minimal outer margin, desktop landscape.
Text (verbatim where prominent): "Settings", "Connections", "Canvas", "Timetable", "Documents", "Upload document", "Transcript", "Academic Work", "Academic calendar", "Version history".
Constraints: no gradients, no glass, no colorful cards, no serif, no decorative eyebrows, no floating short dividers, no nested card stack, no invented analytics beyond obvious placeholder values, internal rules full bleed, neutral and indigo system only except Canvas vendor red.
